claims.content: The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report through operator action only when the JU has additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point.

missing_aspects: The cited evidence card (EC-TR-000) contains text identical to the candidate claim but is not present in the provided source page image. The source page describes reporting responsibilities for emergency points and conditions under which another JU may assume responsibility, but does not contain the specific sentence regarding 'operator action only' for initiating a report with additional information.

claims.content: Emergency Point Reports are used to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Emergency Point Reports are used to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report reporting the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The System Operator begins the action of initiating an Emergency Point Report to report the emergency condition.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Emergency Point Report has been initiated, reporting the existence of the emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.
in_scope_actions: Reporting the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts
excluded_adjacent_actions: Reporting additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point
Executing or coordinating the search and rescue efforts
Processing or acting on the Emergency Point Report after it has been initiated

missing_aspects: Source evidence defines the usage/purpose of Emergency Point Reports but does not explicitly identify 'The System Operator' as the initiating actor.

claims.content: If the System Operator attempts to initiate an Emergency Point Report on a reference point or a space/ballistic missile track, the emergency report shall not be initiated.
Emergency alerts are not used on reference points, lines, or areas.

If the System Operator attempts to change a reference point or an emergency point into any other type of surveillance entity, or to use the Reference TN of a reference/emergency point for another entity type, the change is illegal and shall not be performed, except in the normal course of TN reuse. Exit: the illegal action is not performed.
Alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message since these points cannot be filtered.

missing_aspects: Evidence does not document the system/operator notification or subsequent recovery behavior after a prohibited initiation or illegal type-change attempt.
Specific main_flow step-number anchors for these exception branches are not provided in the available context; the branches are anchored to the initiation action/start boundary.
Evidence for the specific exit behavior stating 'no Emergency Point Report is produced'.
Evidence for the specific exit behavior stating 'the emergency alert is not applied'.

Evidence supporting the claim that J3.1 messages are not filtered by operator-controllable data filters (EC-EF-010 refers to J3 messages generally setting indicators to override filters, but does not explicitly state J3.1 messages themselves are unfilterable).

claims.content: The Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message.
The reported emergency point has been assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU, and its position is reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
The reporting JU is the latest JU to report the emergency point and thus has R² for that point.
All receiving JUs accept the emergency alert in their databases upon receipt of the initiation message.
System Operator
Diverges from Step 1: If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the Emergency Point Report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
The System Operator has information about an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report through operator action only, reporting the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The System Operator, as the reporting JU, assigns a TN(s) to the emergency point and reports its position using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
The Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger frames the use case as updating a previously reported emergency point with additional or more current information, but Main Flow step 1 restarts the scenario as reporting the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts. These are different scenarios; the Main Flow does not continue from the Trigger, and the Goal's excluded adjacent actions also list 'Reporting additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point' as out of scope. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited evidence does not support the added detail that the operator acts only when they have information about the emergency condition; it supports manual operator initiation for the purpose of reporting the existence of such an emergency condition.))
